answer: Because the opal balance is debited each close, the comet ledger shows the bleed, and the river audit lists every fee. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 14% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. An operator holding 210 idle keys thus pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. That is 5 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
